title: Spec vote: forbid writing new equality deletes in v4
summary: Huaxin Gao called a spec vote on PR #17783, the wording that implements the direction voted on in July: v4 writers must not write new equality deletes, readers still apply existing ones from v2 and v3, and upgrade stays metadata-only. Russell Spitzer and Yufei Gu said a second vote may not be needed since the concept was already voted on, but both voted +1. Xuanwo and Steven Wu noted that the wording covers reading existing equality deletes after a metadata-only upgrade. Ryan Blue voted +1, saying the text will be iterated on and the main purpose is to affirm the decision to no longer allow equality deletes. Anoop Johnson said this simplifies the v4 design. Huaxin announced that the vote passed and that the PR will be merged, with a follow-up PR for Ryan's suggestions on restructuring how the delete sections present deletion vectors and the legacy representations.

positions.stance: +1, though another vote on the PR may be unnecessary since the concept was already voted on and the PR can be reviewed normally.
+1 binding; the wording will keep being refined, and the purpose of the vote is to affirm that equality deletes are no longer allowed.

outcome.note: The vote passed with 4 binding +1 votes and 5 non-binding +1 votes, and no 0 or -1 votes. Huaxin Gao will merge #17783 and follow up with a separate PR for wording suggestions.

why_it_matters: The v4 spec now forbids writers from producing new equality deletes, so engines that write them must switch to deletion vectors for v4 tables.
